lines.en: : ...and thus the battle raged on!
: It’s been raging on for hours now! I want to go to sleep!

: Muffled by the sounds of dirt and gravel, Nithhala’s voice is unable to reach Der Krampus! And, with a whip of his tail, he sends a shockwave through the air that deals 5 points of damage to everyone!
: Or...everyone but Nithhala, I suppose. She manages to avoid it since she’s currently lying face down in the soil.
: Hooraaaaaay.
: Perhaps the problem is that we’re trying to fight the Krampus at all? Maybe if we banded together and taught him the true meaning of Christmas, he’d be more reluctant to hurt us?
: Sensing a sickening feeling of hope and splendor, Der Krampus changes targets and sets his sight on Xessaxia!
: What?! But it’s not even his turn! And Zagull has done far more to provoke him than I have! Isn’t that right, Zagull?!
: Zagull?
: Hm? What?
: As Der Krampus gazes at the satyr’s voluptuous and somewhat goat-ish figure, he chuckles to himself, reaching into his burlap sack and removing a tiny snowglobe.
: With the globe in one hand and a large, birch rod in the other, a snarl crawls across his face — a yellowish snaggletooth peeking outward as he speaks.
: Have you been a good girl?...Or have you been a bad girl?

: Just say it, Futaba. It’s clear this fight isn’t going to end until we play along with whatever this Krampus guy wants. So just satisfy Molly’s secret fetish to hear you call yourself a good and/or bad girl.
: It is for Der Krampus, not me.
: I’ve been a bad girl.
: Wha- no. Ram, Der Krampus is speaking to Xessaxia right now.
: I’ve been a very, very bad girl.
: You’d crawl right back to your hole if you only knew the things I’ve done with ghosts.
: What? You’re a bard, not a warlock. What do ghosts have do with anything?
: Nithhala gets up.
: Nithhala can’t get up unless she succeeds on her death saving rolls or is helped by an ally.
: She does it anyway. It’s a Christmas miracle.
: Damn it. I forgot I added that mechanic into tonight’s game. Fine. Nithhala is no longer downed. But her Christmas miracle is on cooldown for the next 365 days.
: What does Nithhala do next?
: Leaves.
: Nithhala turns her back to Der Krampus in an effort to escape, prompting him take an opportunity attack against her!
: Hah...
: With one hand still holding tightly onto the snowglobe, Der Krampus uses his other to swing his birch rod at Nithhala!
: With a violent crack, it snaps against the back of her neck for fifteen points of damage! She’s downed again!
: Ugh! Really? My Christmas miracle didn’t even bring me back to full HP?! That’s no miracle! That’s a lucky coincidence.
: Fine. I’ll play along. Xessaxia steps toward Der Krampus and seductively raises her eyebrow at him. I’ve been a very good girl, Mr. Krampus...don’t you believe me?...she says.
: Are you trying to seduce him?...
: I don’t know what I’m supposed to do! This fight keeps dragging on and on no matter what we do and he doesn’t look any weaker than he did when we started!
: I wish Ami and Maya were here. Molly probably forgot to re-tune the fight to compensate for our missing party members.
: False. Arborea and Racerrk have been separated from the party for several sessions now and won’t be able to return until they restore order in the Western Sanctum.
: What happened to Urrheak?
: He’s been dead since last Christmas, Ram. Racerrk is his long-lost child who has dedicated his life to avenging his father. How many times must you be reminded of this?
: If Urrheak is the father, who is the mother?
: Oh! Lidearel!
: What an unexpected plot twist. This is why you are the master of dungeons, Emerald Guardian.
: What? No. Lidearel isn’t the mother. I was merely rejoicing at the fact that she has finally arrived.
: Even the plot twist has a twist to it. I am on the edge of my seat.
: Sorry for the holdup, everyone. Touka and her mom showed up at Sensei’s place, so I wound up getting roped into teaching them about regular people again.
: I brought ice cream, though. And energy drinks for anyone who wants them. What’d I miss?
: The birth of your child, you heathen.
: Wow. I didn’t realize I’d been gone that long.
: What happened to Rin? Is she asleep already?
: No, but I should be! This is the longest fight of my life. And I dated Otoha for like a whole year, so that’s saying something.
: Well, what are we fighting against exactly? Another one of Thaum’s emissaries? Or did Zagull just accidentally start another bar fight?
: We’re locked in a heated battle with Der Crumpet.
: Krampus, Kendo Princess. Crumpets are an English pastry.
: That makes him all the more threatening. Everyone knows how bad English food is.
: That...
: You don’t...
: S-Silence! I have to fill Lidearel in on what she’s missed out on!
: We showed up for a festival. Der Crumpet popped out. Now Futaba is trying to fuck him.
: Not even close, Nithhala!
: Xessaxia is trying to fuck him.
: Hah...
: I wonder...what it would be like...with a satyr...
: If you’re truly curious, I can forward you several resources once the game comes to a close. But for now, the recap is as such-
: With Racerrk and Arborea currently tying up Urrheak’s loose ends in the Western Sanctum, the remainder of the party has decided to take it easy for the time being.
: Or at least that was the intention.
: Upon hearing the news of an annual holiday festival in a nearby town, you’ve taken up residence at their inn and have decided to spend the winter there as you await your friends.

: To fill both the lull in time and the abyss that has become your coffers, you’ve accepted several commissions from locals. But there was one commission in particular that sounded far too good to be true.
: And, as I’m sure you know, when something sounds too good to be true, it is almost always because it is.
: The mission — decorate a market stall to prepare for the holiday festival! The reward — 10 gold pieces each.
: The outcome — some Christmas demon wants to kill us now.
: That is essentially true, yes.
: He popped out from behind the stall once we showed up to decorate it.
: Now he won’t let us go until we defeat him. But he refuses to actually kill us and just keeps downing us before healing us himself.
: And now you’re...trying to have sex with him?
: Only because he looked like he was going to kill me when I tried to teach him about Christmas! It’s not like I want to spend 2:00 AM roleplaying a satyr making love to Der Krampus!
: I’ll do it if you don’t want to.
: For the party, of course.
: That solves nothing!
: We won’t know that until we try.
: I will inform you now that Der Krampus does not intend to have sex with anyone tonight.
: We really won’t know that until we try, though.
: Do you have any thoughts on how to tackle this, Tsuneyo?
: I have already tried to tackle it. The attempt resulted in me being thrown into a nearby fountain. But as your character is a rogue and not a bard, it is possible you will have more success.
: He’s also holding a snowglobe thingy. Molly drew a lot of attention to it twice now, so it’s probably important in some way.
: The snowglobe is merely a diversion. We all know the true evil in this battle lies within British cuisine. Ram summons celebrity chef, Gordon Ramsay. How many dice must I roll to do this?
: None. Der Krampus laid out an anti-Ramsay forcefield before the battle started.
: Damn it. He’s thought of everything.
: Lidearel knows he’s holding this snowglobe thing? She can see it?
: Correct. The globe is visible to all of you and about the same size as a human head.
: Got it. Then, whose turn is it now and when do I come in?
: You’ll enter combat after Zagull Throat Spear, who takes his turn next. I rolled initiative for you prior to your arrival and have been acting in your place since.
: Gotcha. I’ll just wait until Sana is done then.
: So it’s my turn now? Did I hear that right?
: Yes. But keep in mind that you’re still currently paralyzed from the waist down due to-
: HEY, FUCKBOY!
: Oh, dear. Here we go again.
: YOU THINK JUST BECAUSE I CAN’T MOVE MY LEGS THAT I WON’T POUND THAT KRAMPUSSY INTO OBLIVION?!
: YOU’VE CROSSED THE PATH OF ZAGULL THROAT SPEAR, DEMON BITCH! AND THE MOMENT THIS PARALYSIS WEARS OFF, I’M SHOVING THAT BIRCH ROD UP YOUR GODDAMN-
: Huh?...Why are you rolling?...What happened?...
: Hm? Oh, nothing. You just took another twenty points of psychic damage from Der Krampus’ “Thought Mirror.” Your arms are paralyzed as well now. Err...sorry. Arm.
: What the heck is “Thought Mirror?!”
: The same ability he used against you the last time you tried shouting at him. It’s why your legs are paralyzed, Sana.
: How did you even forget something that only happened like ten minutes ago?
: YOU’D DAMN WELL KNOW THE ANSWER TO THAT IF YOU WERE IN MY SHOES!!!!
: STOP YELLING! I WAS ABOUT TO FALL ASLEEP!
: NO ONE SLEEPS UNTIL DER CRUMP...KRAMPUS IS DEFEATED!
: I AM ALSO YELLING NOW!
: And I am going to use Sleight of Hand to try and steal that snowglobe thing now that Zagull is fully paralyzed.
: ROLL FOR D- Ahem. Roll for dexterity.
: Kachow. Natural 20.
: Distracted by the curvaceous figure of the female satyr and elated by Zagull Throat Spear’s full-body paralysis, Der Krampus doesn’t even notice Lidereal as she makes a break for the snowglobe!
: The speed at which she moves almost makes it seem as if she’s fading in and out of existence!
: Visible to no one but her, a set of red, feathery wings blossom out of her spine- but disappear just as quickly as they formed!
: It isn’t until she begins to scale the demon’s body that he notices her presence! But, by the time he does, it’s already too late!
: She leaps backward — clutching the snowglobe with both hands. It seems gigantic in her possession when, just moments ago, the demon made it seem so small.
: She gazes into the globe- and among the white flecks...between those lit-up houses...she notices what appears to be small figures of her and her companions. But they look different. Older.
: Der Krampus does not chase after. He straightens his posture. It’s the closest to human that he’s ever looked.
: He abandons his thoughts of the satyr’s breasts. He abandons his glee at the damage inflicted to the brute. And he locks his eyes on the halfling rogue.
: “Are you a good girl...or a bad girl?” he asks, snarling violently as a grin spreads across his face.
: I gaze back at him and smirk, pressing one of my cheeks up against the globe before winking at him.
: That’s for me to know and you to find out.
: Then I smash it on the ground with all of my strength.
: A blanket of endless white, purer than the snow itself, covers the party and overtakes everything.
: For a moment, there is nothing but silence. Silence so great that even the sounds of their labored breathing fall upon the deafest of ears.
: “Is this death?” is the only thought that finds its way into each of your heads — but it’s only for a moment.
: That endless white fades. And, when it does, you’re back at the inn.
: There’s an old man in a red suit...reading a story to a group of children seated in a semi-circle with their hands clasped together.
: They look scared. But they also look intrigued.
: You find each other. You realize you’ve all come back from the same place.
: But before any of you can muster any words at all, the old man’s voice fills the room.
: “Are you a good girl...or a bad girl?”
: “I have something for both.”
Lidearel has leveled up!
